==English== {{wp|}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|tĕl|a=UK,GA}}, {{IPA|en|/tɛl/|[tʰɛɫ]|[tʰɛl]}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-tell.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{audio|en|en-us-tell.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛl|s=1}} * {{hmp|en|tail|tale}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|tellen|t=to count, tell}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tellan|t=to count, tell}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*talljan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*taljaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*talzijaną|t=to count, enumerate}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*talą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*talō|t=number, counting}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dol-|t=calculation, fraud}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|tälle|t=to say; tell}}, {{cog|fy|telle|t=to count}}, {{cog|fy|fertelle|t=to tell, narrate}}, {{cog|nl|tellen|t=to count}} and {{cog|nl|vertellen|t=to tell}}, {{cog|nds|tellen|t=to count}}, {{cog|de|zählen}}, {{cog|fo|telja}}, {{cog|sv|tala|t=to speak}}. More at [[tale]]. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|told,~ed,tolled}} # ''Mental senses related to determining, reckoning, or perceiving ## {{lb|en|transitive|archaic|_|outside of idioms}} To determine the [[number]], [[amount]], or [[value]] of [''something'']. ##: {{syn|en|count|reckon|enumerate}} ##: {{ux|en|[[all told|All '''told''']], there were over a dozen.  Can you [[tell time|'''tell''' time]] on a clock?  He had '''[[untold]]''' wealth.}} ##* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|II|vii|text=And in his lap a masse of coyne he '''told''',
And turned vpsidowne, to feede his eye
A couetous desire with his huge threasury.}} ##* {{RQ:Marlowe Jew of Malta|13|I|text=Well fare the Arabians, who so richly pay
The things they traffic for with wedge of gold,
Whereof a man may easily in a day
'''Tell''' that which may maintain him all his life.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1875|author=Hugh MacMillan|journal=The Sunday Magazine |passage=Only He who made them can '''tell''' the number of the stars, and mark the place of each in the order of the one great dominant spiral.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive}} To [[notice]], [[discern]]. (''Roughly, "can tell" means "know" but with a sense of direct perception.'') ##: {{ux|en|I can '''tell''' that you're thrilled.}} ##: {{ux|en|You can '''tell''' you've struck a nerve when even the crowd stops laughing.}} ##: {{ux|en|She couldn't '''tell''' the words on the chalkboard without her glasses.}} ##* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|text=Captain Edward Carlisle, soldier as he was, martinet as he was, felt a curious sensation of helplessness seize upon him as he met her steady gaze, her alluring smile; he could not '''tell''' what this prisoner might do.}} ### To pick up on a difference. (''See ''[[tell apart]]'' for more''.) ###: {{ux|en|An expert can '''tell''' an original from a forgery.}} ###: {{ux|en|Can you '''tell''' whether those flowers are real or silk, from this distance?  No, there's no way to '''tell'''.}} ###*: Whether she loves me or loves me not / Sometimes it's hard to '''tell''' # ''Social senses of communicating'' ## {{lb|en|transitive|ditransitive}} To [[narrate]], to [[recount]]. ##: {{ux|en|I want to '''tell''' a story;  I want to '''tell''' you a story.}} ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=7|passage=“{{...}}Churchill, my dear fellow, we have such greedy sharks, and wolves in lamb's clothing. Oh, dear, there's so much to '''tell''' you, so many warnings to give you, but all that must be postponed for the moment.”}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|ditransitive}} To [[convey]] by [[speech]]; to [[say]]. ##: {{ux|en|Finally, someone '''told''' him the truth.  He seems to like to '''tell''' lies.}} ##* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=4|passage=I '''told''' him about everything I could think of; and what I couldn't think of he did. He asked about six questions during my yarn, but every question had a point to it. At the end he bowed and thanked me once more. As a thanker he was main-truck high; I never see anybody so polite.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[instruct]] or [[inform]]. ##: {{ux|en|Please '''tell''' me how to do it.}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|Genesis|xii|18|text=Why didst thou not '''tell''' me that she was thy wife?}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=But Miss Thorn relieved the situation by laughing aloud,{{...}}. We began to '''tell''' her about Mohair and the cotillon, and of our point of observation from the Florentine galleried porch, and she insisted she would join us there.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[order]]; to [[direct]], to say to someone. ##: {{ux|en|'''Tell''' him to go away.}} ##* {{RQ:Wells Ann Veronica|passage=She said she hoped she had not distressed him by the course she had felt obliged to take, and he '''told''' her not to be a fool.}} ##* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2012-10-25|author=John Noble Wilford|title=Neil Armstrong, First Man on the Moon, Dies at 82|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2012/08/26/science/space/neil-armstrong-dies-first-man-on-moon.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 |passage=Stability was restored, but once the re-entry propulsion was activated, the crew was '''told''' to prepare to come home before the end of their only day in orbit.}} ## {{label|en|transitive}} To use ([[bead]]s or similar objects) as an aid to [[prayer]]. ## {{lb|en|intransitive|childish}} To inform someone in authority about a wrongdoing. ##: {{syn|en|tell on}} ##: {{ux|en|I saw you steal those sweets! I'm '''telling'''!}} ## {{label|en|authorship|intransitive}} To reveal information in [[prose]] through [[outright]] [[expository]] [[statement]] — contrasted with ''[[show]]''. ##: {{ux|en|Maria rewrote the section of her novel that talked about Meg and Sage's friendship to have less '''telling''' and more showing.}} # ''Abstract senses related to showing or revealing'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To show, be showing, be revealed. ##* '''1990''', {{w|Stephen Coonts}}, Under Siege, 1991 {{w|Pocket Books}} edition, {{ISBN|0671742949}}, p.409: ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[reveal]]. ##: {{ux|en|Time will '''tell''' what became of him.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have an effect, especially a noticeable one; to be apparent, to be demonstrated. ##: {{ux|en|Sir Gerald was moving slower; his wounds were beginning to '''tell'''.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 18, 2011|author=Ben Dirs|work=BBC Sport |title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/rugby_union/14959055.stm Rugby World Cup 2011: England 41-10 Georgia] |passage=But England's superior fitness '''told''' in the second half, with Delon Armitage, Manu Tuilagi and Chris Ashton (two) going over for tries to secure a bonus-point win.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} (of a fact) To support a certain position. ##* {{RQ:Mill On Liberty|passage=Opinion ought [… to give] merited honour to every one, whatever opinion he may hold{{...}}keeping nothing back which '''tells''', or can be supposed to '''tell''', in their favour.}} =====Usage notes===== * Sense group 1 is now most often found with words bearing a sense of ability, such as "can tell" or "one way to tell". * For many of the senses of ''tell'', the word ''show'' would have a contrasting meaning, and in other senses, it would have a nearly identical meaning. * In dialects, other past tense forms (besides ''told'') may be found, including {{m|en|tald}}/{{m|en|tauld}} {{q|Scotland}}, {{m|en|tawld}} {{q|Devonshire}}, {{m|en|teld}} {{q|Yorkshire|Devonshire}}, {{m|en|telled}} {{q|Northern England, Scotland, and in nonstandard speech # A reflexive, often habitual behavior, {{non-gloss|especially}} one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under psychological stress (such as a [[poker]] game or Wang; Grant Cornett|title=Inside the Delirious Rise of ‘Superfake’ Handbags|date=2023-05-04|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/04/magazine/celine-chanel-gucci-superfake-handbags.html|passage=Those whose business it is to verify luxury bags insist, at least publicly, that there’s always a “'''tell'''” to a superfake.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260102010244/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/04/magazine/celine-chanel-gucci-superfake-handbags.html|archivedate=2 January 2026}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} That which is told; a [[tale]] or [[account]]. #* '''April 4, 1743''', {{w|Horace Walpole}}, ''letter to Sir Horace Mann'' # {{lb|en|internet}} A [[private]] [[message]] to an individual in a [[chat room]]; a [[whisper]]. =====See also===== * {{l|en|dead giveaway}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{der|en|ar|تَلّ||hill, elevation}} or {{der|en|he|תֵּל||tr=tél|hill}}, from {{uder|en|sem-pro|*tall-||hill}}. {{root|en|ar|ت ل ل}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q755017}}{{lb|en|archaeology}} A [[hill]] or [[mound]], originally and especially in the Middle East, over or consisting of the ruins of ancient settlements. =====Translations===== {{trans-top|A hill or mound}} * Arabic: * French: * Hebrew: * Italian: * Latin: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t|ru|телль}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{cln|en|control verbs|ditransitive verbs|irregular verbs|reporting verbs}} {{C|en|Talking}}
